documentation.title: API Noxacloud
documentation.subtitle: A complete reference for Noxacloud's endpoints, with authentication, real request and response examples, and the order, scheduling, and billing flows used day-to-day in integration. Each endpoint shows the accepted parameters, the expected request body, and a response example for every possible status code, including the most common error cases. The documentation is split into public APIs, which don't require an access key, and client APIs, for authenticated integrations with your system.

auth.intro: Logging in (POST /v1/auth/login) sets two httpOnly cookies: access_token, short-lived, and refresh_token, which renews access without requiring another login once the first expires. These two cookies are enough for public endpoints. Client endpoints also require the Authorization: Bearer <API key> header, generated in the dashboard, which identifies the call by integration and lets you revoke it without affecting the client's logged-in session.
auth.accessToken: httpOnly cookie, expires in 15 minutes. Used on every API call.
auth.refreshToken: httpOnly cookie, expires in 30 days. Only used on /v1/auth/refresh.
auth.bearerToken: API key generated in the dashboard, sent via header. Only required on client endpoints.

endpoints.publicIntro: Public endpoints only require the httpOnly session cookies (access_token and refresh_token), no API key.
endpoints.clientIntro: Client endpoints require the session cookies plus the Authorization: Bearer <API key> header, generated in the client dashboard.
